name: Jaguar Health, Inc.

profile.description: Jaguar Health is a commercial-stage pharmaceutical company focused on plant-based, sustainably sourced medicines derived from the crofelemer compound harvested from the Amazon rainforest. Lead product Mytesi is FDA-approved for HIV-associated diarrhea; in early 2026 the company licensed U.S. commercial rights to Future Pak and is now concentrating on rare intestinal-failure indications (MVID and short bowel syndrome) through its Napo Pharmaceuticals subsidiary. The company has executed repeated reverse stock splits, most recently 1-for-15 effective September 17, 2026, to maintain its Nasdaq listing, and has a market capitalization of roughly $4M.

innovation.label: WEAK
innovation.analysis: Innovation Track Record (1/3): The Future Pak license generated $19.1M of license revenue in Q1 2026, but product revenue fell ~45% that quarter and total Q2 revenue fell 59% to ~$1.2M, so no new product has opened a durable revenue stream [2][3]. AI Deployment (0/2): No AI products or quantified AI savings were found in filings or releases [4]. Market Share Leadership (0/2): Mytesi is a niche product whose sales are shrinking [3]. Product Pipeline (1/2): Crofelemer powder for oral solution is in development for MVID and SBS intestinal failure, but the company gives no firm regulatory timelines [1]. R&D Intensity (1/1): FY2025 R&D of $25.0M was 217% of $11.5M revenue, well above peers [5].

inspiration.label: DEVELOPING
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (3/4): Jaguar's mission of developing novel, sustainably derived plant-based medicines from rainforest botanicals is specific and distinctive, though not yet validated by commercial success [4][6]. Community Impact (1/2): Founder-CEO Lisa Conte received a 2021 Pure Earth Impact Award for work with Indigenous communities in the Amazon, but no dollar-quantified programs were found [4]. Employee Retention (0/2): No retention or tenure data was found, and repeated dilution and cost-cutting point to instability [2]. Insider Buying (0/2): No meaningful open-market insider purchases were found.

infrastructure.label: WEAK
infrastructure.analysis: Calculated on the Growth-sleeve formula; forward PEG was unavailable and excluded (8 weight units). D/E of 253% is near the 300% floor (0.20), and ROE of -549%, a -130.9% profit margin, a negative forward P/E (-0.29) and Q2 YoY revenue growth of -58.9% all score 0 [7]. The only positive is the FY2020-FY2025 revenue CAGR of 4.2% (derived from $9.39M to $11.51M reported revenue), which scores 0.61 at 2x weight, giving 1.79/10, rounded to 2 [5]. The stock passes the liquidity floor on reported average volume (2.12M x $1.62 = ~$3.4M/day), but recent volume of ~0.70M shares implies only ~$1.1M/day, which is near the $1M threshold [7].

ai_resilience.label: MODERATE
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (6/9): Crofelemer is an FDA-approved botanical drug with a complex natural-product supply chain and orphan-indication regulatory pathways, which AI cannot replicate or substitute directly [1][6]. The longer-term exposure is that AI-accelerated drug discovery lowers barriers for competing GI and intestinal-failure therapies, and a ~$4M market-cap company has little capacity to respond. AI Opportunity (0/1): No AI-related revenue was found [4].

infinite_game.summary: Jaguar has a genuinely distinctive cause in rainforest-derived, plant-based medicine, carried by a founder-CEO with more than a decade at the helm. Survival financing, repeated reverse splits and collapsing product revenue have pushed it into a quarter-to-quarter fight to stay listed. Sinek would admire the cause but see an organization forced into a finite game by its balance sheet.

just_cause.analysis: The commitment to sustainably sourced, plant-based medicines and partnerships with Indigenous Amazon communities is a distinctive, service-oriented cause that has persisted under founder Lisa Conte, CEO since 2013 [4][6]. It has not been validated by commercial success, and the company now depends on licensing its core product to Future Pak [3].

trusting_teams.analysis: No Glassdoor or retention data was found, and the organization has operated under constant financing pressure with repeated reverse splits, including 1-for-15 in September 2026 [1][4]. That environment rarely supports the psychological safety Sinek describes.

worthy_rivals.analysis: No management commentary framing competitors as worthy rivals was found. Communication focuses on the company's own unique botanical status rather than learning from peers [6].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Jaguar has repositioned from commercializing Mytesi itself to licensing U.S. rights to Future Pak and focusing on orphan intestinal-failure indications, a real model change [1][3]. The shift was driven largely by financial necessity rather than proactively by the cause.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Leadership raised R&D from $16.5M in FY2024 to $25.0M in FY2025 even as revenue was flat, prioritizing rare-disease programs over near-term losses [5]. That commitment was funded through heavy shareholder dilution, which tempers the credit.

investment_thesis: Jaguar's only real asset is crofelemer, an FDA-approved botanical drug now being developed for ultrarare intestinal-failure indications (MVID, SBS) where approved options are scarce [1]. The Future Pak license brought in $19.1M of license revenue in Q1 2026 and shifts U.S. commercialization costs off Jaguar's books [3].
thesis_continued: Financial distress dominates the investment case. Q2 2026 revenue fell 59%, FY2025 net loss was $53.4M on $11.5M revenue, D/E is 253%, and the September 2026 1-for-15 reverse split was done expressly to keep the Nasdaq listing [1][2][5]. A pipeline success would need to arrive before the next financing round dilutes shareholders further.
key_catalysts: Regulatory progress for crofelemer powder in MVID or SBS intestinal failure, which could unlock orphan-drug value [1]
Additional license or milestone payments from the Future Pak agreement following the $19.1M recognized in Q1 2026 [3]
Restored compliance with Nasdaq listing standards after the September 17, 2026 reverse split [1]
key_risks: Ongoing dilution and potential Nasdaq delisting; the company has relied on serial reverse splits to stay listed [1]
Product revenue is collapsing: Q2 2026 total revenue was ~$1.2M, down 59% YoY [2]
Trading liquidity is thin; recent daily traded value of ~$1.1M sits near IOWN's $1M liquidity floor [7]
